title: Joe Wynn skips town, Pete Raphael joins, and the vote not to go farther into Florida
summary: Wynn disappears over money trouble, Chinee Foster and then cousin Pete drum, the Jacksonville dance goes badly then wins crowds, and the band votes to return, a decision Sayles calls a mistake.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: I don't know whether he might be Eagle Eye Shields, but he was the leader of that band. Edmund Hall played with Eagle Eye Shields. Well, I'm going to get to that, Edmund Hall was at, now I ain't going to Jacksonville, but the band was consistent of, like I told you, I go back to Joy Morris on trombone, the band on trumpet, Edmund Washington on sax and clandered, Edmund Hall on sax and clandered, Albert Morgan on bass. Oh, I forgot to tell you how I went, Joy Wynn, Joy Wynn had left, had left. And that's why we hired, I forgot to see how you get tangled up, is that all right? Yeah, that's okay, don't worry. No, look, Joy Wynn left us, he got into some kind of finance trouble with Mr. Earl and Dr. Grundy, and he skipped out of town, and Chinese was round town, and we used Chinese. We used Chinese until my cousin came back. My cousin, we finally got my cousin Pete Redfield in the band, just like we had promised, we said when we get over there and find our way around, we were supposed to find Joy, we couldn't find Joy Wynn because he had his hand in with the big balls, you see. So he finally had to leave town, and we used Chinese a while, because he was around, like I said, different bands were coming in, and like I said, that was where she was living there, I said I met Sadie. Well, we had this woman, Helen Jackson, playing piano with us, and I couldn't think of the other woman we had before, the first one was there. Well anyhow, just before this trip to going to Jacksonville, Pete Redfield, my cousin got in the band. And Pete came up there, and he still had that little grudge against us, I don't know, that was his way. And we got him a place to stay, and Pete got a good friend with the landlady, and they got to be, what you say, sweethearts in their voice. And we had a lot of trouble with Pete and his drinking. Pete would get drunk and mess up and everything, and then sometimes we had to go to look for him. Well anyhow, on this trip, he was on this trip with us to Florida, I'm not sure. And like I said, when we got to Jacksonville, Florida, the place that we were supposed to play, Eagle Eye wouldn't let us work there. But we waked at Somersonic Hall, I remember, and the dance didn't go so good. And we had to wake with another band, that's my wife. They had one of those things like they had Mobile, they had a brass band playing for the people to dance by. And it was a good brass band. But when the people heard us, which they was called the Pensacola Jazz, then, that New Orleans swing and that New Orleans music we was playing, they just went wild over it. And that still kept Eagle Eye from having us playing in this place, you see. So we played a few towns out of Jackson. I remember one of the towns, I remember well, let's see now, I believe it was Olanda. I played that particular town, I remember well. And the people who had a nice crowd with me, nice, nice money on that deal. And I noticed, in all those places going out way down that way, the colored people, they get very excited. They used to drink that moonshine and thing, you know, and man, they would, it was a different kind of colored people like in New Orleans, you know, they were ready to fight and everything. And they had, they still had that eye out in the head where if you play hot, you have to play fast. But after listening to us, and the New Orleans music we're playing, they kind of caught the eye out in the way, you don't have to play fast, you know what I mean? You can still be playing hot and still be playing in a groovy tempo, you see. So getting to that same trip, so Joy and Morty, we had a meeting on the band, we're not here long. And we were what they called pro-starled and everything to vote on who wanted to go down further and who wanted to go back. Well, some of the fellas began to get a little discouraged, you know. They wanted to go back to Pensacola because we weren't making the money we thought we were going to make, you know. And the vote went against Joy of going down further in Florida, down south. I remember he mentioned Panama City and Miami and those places. And that was one of the biggest mistakes we made. Because if we had to went down there, which I found out later, because there were bands coming from that that made families like Belton, and there was another band that even went to New York, back there in the 30s. Well, those guys, and this was back in 24 and 25 I'm telling you about, you see. But at that time those guys hadn't picked up on that New Orleans piece. See, we would have made us a fortune of money.
